page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the high clock speed family, powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores via two threads per core on an x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA. It is provisioned with 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on remote block storage and standard host resources alongside a 20 Gbps baseline network capability.

Benchmark evaluations reveal robust computational and memory throughput capabilities. Multi-core performance is highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 49036.54 and an extended instructions score of 57136.8, alongside 269.5 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and a strong large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 209.21 GB/sec. Database operations in PassMark reached 22550.06, while Redis sustained 57.01 million operations per second. In contrast, text generation in large language model inference shows diminished efficiency, generating 56.49 tokens per second on a 135M model and 8.69 tokens per second on a 7B model due to the absence of dedicated matrix or GPU accelerators.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation positions this server efficiently for CPU-bound enterprise deployments that prioritize core density over excessive RAM pools. Because local NVMe storage is absent, disk I/O performance relies on network-attached storage. The platform is well suited for multi-threaded compilation tasks, compute-heavy batch processing, distributed caching tiers, and relational database servers that can operate within a 128 GB memory boundary.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance equipped with 64 dedicated vCPUs from a 32-core Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM configuration, it integrates 128 GB of system memory, alongside 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate upper-tier capabilities in multi-threaded integer and decompression workloads, recording 269.5 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, strong large-block read memory bandwidth of 209.21 GB/sec, and high PassMark extended instruction metrics. Conversely, generative LLM text processing is constrained by reliance on standard vector extensions without discrete accelerators. This profile makes the instance well suited for CPU-intensive computing, Clang software builds, distributed caching, and mid-sized transactional databases requiring high core counts.
